newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-DUNN RETAINS MEN'S 400 INDIVIDUAL MEDLEY WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-DUNN RETAINS MEN'S 400 INDIVIDUAL MEDLEY WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Australia's Matthew Dunn retained his world short-course 400 metres individual medley title with a runaway victory in the final on Thursday.
Commonwealth champion Dunn turned the rest into also-rans as he carved out a huge lead early in the race in the 25-metre Scandinavium arena pool and broke his own championship record in victory.

Dunn won by nearly six seconds in four minutes 6.89 seconds and has every chance of repeating the golden individual medley double he completed at the 1995 world short-course championships in Rio de Janeiro.
A mere 0.01 seconds separated the next three swimmers, with China's Xie Xufeng taking the silver in 4:12.52.
Germany's Christian Keller and American Ron Karnaugh each claimed bronze medals, both clocking 4:12.53.

American Chad Carvin returned the second-fastest time in the morning's heats but was disqualified after stroke judges at both ends of the pool ruled that his hands did not enter the water simultaneously on the opening butterfly leg.
